picks.title: PayAuthors.com: Are your books in pirate libraries?
picks.excerpt: PayAuthors.com is a new website and service that lets authors check whether their books appear in pirate libraries used to train AI models.
picks.rationale: A new service authors can use right away: PayAuthors.com checks whether a book sits in the pirate libraries used for AI training.

picks.title: Fish Audio Launches Drama 3 to Direct AI Voices and Edit a Single Word
picks.excerpt: Fish Audio's Drama 3 TTS lets producers direct AI voice performances in plain language and re-record a single mis-stressed word, pitched at audiobook and audio-drama production.
picks.rationale: A new product release for audiobook makers: Drama 3 takes voice direction in plain language and can re-record a single word, so producers don't have to regenerate the whole take.

picks.title: [단독] 구글도 韓 책 구매한다는데…AI 학습 저작권 강화 법안 ‘낮잠’
picks.excerpt: 앤트로픽에 이어 구글도 국내 출판사를 상대로 도서 구매 계약을 추진하는 것으로 나타났지만, AI 학습 저작권을 강화하는 법안은 국회에서 멈춰 있다.
picks.rationale: A new actor in the AI book-buying story: Google is now pursuing purchase contracts with Korean publishers, following Anthropic, while the bill to tighten AI-training copyright has stalled.

picks.title: Halo's co-creator wrote a novel about AI taking over the world
picks.excerpt: Bungie co-founder Jason Jones has written a novel about AI taking over the world; The Verge runs an excerpt chapter.
picks.rationale: A new book announcement: Bungie co-founder Jason Jones's AI-takeover novel debuts with an excerpt chapter. It is a cultural angle that differs from the tooling and copyright picks.

picks.title: Guest Post – Artificial Intelligence in Scholarly Publishing: Are We Moving Faster Than the Evidence?
picks.excerpt: A guest post argues the next phase of AI adoption in scholarly publishing workflows needs more evaluation, collaboration and human judgment.
picks.rationale: Covers the scholarly-publishing side: it asks for evidence before AI goes further into editorial workflows. It is a different article and argument from the 10-16 agentic-consumption post.

https://www.sedaily.com/article/20103000.new_action: Google (a new buyer, after Anthropic) is pursuing book-purchase contracts with Korean publishers; reported exclusively along with the stalled AI-training copyright bill
